content:
Alex: heads-up — saw a perf regression on Mixtral-8B with our YARN RoPE variant when hitting 32k+ seq. latency jumps ~2.3x for tail tokens compared to NTK/linear runs. profiling attached below.
Maria: ugh. is this only on Mixtral or also on Mistral/Qwen?
Alex: primarily Mixtral so far. ran quick smoke on Mistral and Qwen — smaller bump (~1.15x) but not as dramatic. seems correlated with head_kv_dim configs and a kernel fallback in the runtime.
Jun: can you paste the hotpath from the profiler (nvprof/nsys or our perf counters)? especially kernels selected for matmul/kv-lookup.
Alex: here's the snippet from sample nsys run (trimmed):

```
Kernel chosen: fused_attn_v2_axpy (fast)  — fallback to fused_attn_generic for head_kv_dim >= 64
Time (fused_attn_v2_axpy): 3.4ms
Time (fused_attn_generic): 7.9ms  <--- triggered on longctx for many batches
KV cache copies: spikes at batch boundary when eviction threshold crossed
Batching util: 65% (lots of small batches due to prefix variation)
```

Alex: note the runtime chooses fused_attn_generic when head_kv_dim mapping ends up misaligned with the blocksize heuristics. YARN/NTK variants change effective rotary frequencies and that surfaces alignment issues.
Sam K: runtime has a conservative kernel-selection path when head_kv_dim % block != 0. we can relax that with flag `--kernels.allow_misaligned=true` but need perf safety check.
Maria: can we reproduce with deterministic inputs and smaller harness? if it's alignment maybe a microbenchmark across head_kv_dim values (32/48/56/64/80) + seq len sweep would show inflection.
Jun: I ran a quick matrix yesterday, results (p99 latency, Mixtral-8B, batch=4):

- head_kv_dim 32: 85ms
- head_kv_dim 48: 92ms
- head_kv_dim 56: 210ms  <-- cliff
- head_kv_dim 64: 88ms
- head_kv_dim 80: 95ms

Jun: cliff at 56 — suggests our kernel tiling falls back for that geometry. Also saw increased KV cache evictions when prefix length distribution had >30% variance.
Alex: that 56 is suspiciously common for some exported Mixtral variants. Q: is fallback triggered by head_kv_dim or combined (heads * head_kv_dim) mapping?
Sam K: fallback logic currently checks inner dim % warp_factor + (heads % warp_align) heuristic. it's a combined condition; one operand can push to fallback.
Maria: immediate mitigations: (1) add a quantile-based batching heuristic to avoid micro-batches when prefix variance is high, (2) run kernel-matching pass that prefers a slightly slower but consistent kernel when batch shapes are heterogeneous to avoid cliffing, (3) add regression test for head_kv_dim=56.
Jun: also worth testing RoPE variant toggle: YARN vs NTK vs linear — wrap each in a small eval harness and measure perplexity delta at 32k vs 4k to ensure quality doesn't degrade when we force different kernels.
Alex: ran quick perplexity check forcing `--kernels.allow_misaligned=true` on Mixtral-8B (eval set 1k tokens): delta < 0.01 perplexity but latency improved by 30% at 32k. Seems promising.
Sam K: good. please open a runtime PR with the flag gated behind config + perf benches. add a canary rollout for Dedicated pools only.
InfraBot: perf-run completed — waves:
- canary pool: 3 machines, runs=120
- avg tail latency before: 320ms
- avg tail latency after (allow_misaligned=true): 230ms
- error rate: unchanged

Maria: next steps: add targeted kernel microbench for head_kv_dim in [48..64], implement quantile batching change, add longctx eval (4k/16k/32k) to nightly perf suite for Mixtral and Mistral.
Alex: I'll file follow-ups: runtime PR, bench harness, and a quick incident playbook note in #incidents if we see recurrence. tagging Jun + Sam K to review the kernel PR.
Jun: will do review then run expanded matrix on Qwen.
Sam K: I'll sketch rollout policy and fallback thresholds.
Alex: thanks team :thumbsup:
